newsitem.title: GERMANY: Indonesian minister "astounded" at Nobel choice.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian minister "astounded" at Nobel choice.

text.p: Indonesian Foreign Minister Ali Alatas said on Friday he was "astounded" that this year's Nobel Peace Prize had gone to East Timorese resistance leader Jose Ramos-Horta, branding him a "political adventurist".

"We think he is a political adventurist, for a while representing a very small minority but...(now) repudiated by the majority of the people of East Timor," he told Reuters Television on a visit to the German city of Hamburg.
Alatas also said Ramos-Hortha could not be compared to previous winners of the prestigious prize.
"I wonder what effect it will lue of earlier Nobel Peace Prizes given to such illustrous people like Mr (Nelson) Mandela and Mr (Yasser) Arafat who have brought peace to real conflicts," he said.
Ramos-Hortha, who lives in exile, was awarded the prize jointly with East Timor's Roman Catholic Bishop Carlos Filipe Ximenes Belo. Alatas did not comment on the bishop.

"He really represents no-one but himself," Alatas said of Ramos-Hortha. "What has he really contributed to peace? On the contrary, I think it is he and his group which started all the trouble for the majority of the East Timorese people."
